title: "Exact-state reuse in bounded parameter fitting"

At the frozen Original Born MEA parameter point, sharing the central state and
its first parameter actions preserves all 160 predicted quantities and
residuals, all 800 physical Jacobian entries and all 800 weighted optimizer
Jacobian entries exactly. The dimensionless weighted objective is
40.20153733056146 on both wheels. This is numerical verification of a bounded
calculation, not physical validation of the MEA model or a completed fit.

## Question, method and inputs

The [owning fitting-cost issue](https://github.com/tannerpolley/ePC-SAFT/issues/129)
asks whether repeated central solves and action preparation can be removed
while keeping physical declarations, observations, residual transformations,
weights, parameter coordinates and numerical tolerances unchanged.
The [bound-set issue](https://github.com/tannerpolley/ePC-SAFT/issues/193)
separately asks whether the held coordinates must be rebuilt when the accepted
weighted gradient changes their membership, including inward release.

[ALG-FIT](../../engine/docs/science/algorithms.md#alg-fit) and the
[fitting formulation](../../engine/docs/regression/science/pure-saturation-regression.md)
own the mathematics. The weighted objective is one half the sum of squared
weighted residuals. The optimizer gradient is the weighted Jacobian transpose
times the weighted residual vector. The physical state is resolved by the
existing equilibrium owner; fitting groups only exactly equal declarations.
Every projection, residual transformation and weight stays with its own row.

The preceding extraction read the independent MEA model-D checkout at
`downstream/.worktrees/MEA-Thermodynamics-121-model-d`, its frozen setup anchors,
`model-d/0-0-S1-40-80C-multistart.json:old-rule.fitted`, and the state packet
with SHA-256
`86f60041b28ec4493729b04c0238f44e86fba4becf33d6ddf47d86b7efb82448`.
The complete parameter record, physical declarations, target definitions,
five physical coordinates, bounds and scales are retained in
[mea-initial.json](inputs/mea-initial.json). Numerical provenance is retained
in [initial-summary.json](results/initial-summary.json).
There are 84 physical states and 160 scalar targets. The single initial
objective uses one allowed iteration and a solver-time limit of one microsecond
to prevent a new fitting trajectory; that limit does not cap the initial
objective work. It is not a convergence experiment.

The recorded commands request one OpenMP and BLAS thread, scheduling priority
10 and the shared numerical lock; [execution.json](results/execution.json)
retains those commands. Effective BLAS thread counts were not independently
measured. The baseline wheel SHA-256 is
`b55665901b881836f90af010c22bd16a51a687a4e83242ab6d7d5d10118e582a`.
The measured candidate wheel is
`4235074a5d264a4a30fa1023bc19b6f82040d1c9a957e0dd712cf3d6cf4e4f74`,
source base `11ee6fbed89b541b01aad90459a941b85f3ef285`, diff SHA-256
`fb37d192d796b3242edab02d62cc7dfef70df18fd00d9e25faf92e325514a0f5`.
The original baseline output was recovered completely from the saved thread
after the computer restart removed temporary files. The candidate was built
and installed in the sole Engine environment before calculation.

The exact numerical rows are retained once in
[baseline-initial.csv](results/baseline-initial.csv) and
[candidate-initial.csv](results/candidate-initial.csv). Columns retain row
order and physical versus optimizer-coordinate derivatives. The candidate
trace records 84 prediction groups, 84 differentiation groups and 84 first-action
batches. Its 132 equilibrium solve calls include preparation and cold fallback;
they are not 132 distinct physical input states. Inclusive span durations
overlap and must not be added to estimate exclusive cost.

CPU time is about 1.97 times lower for this one initial evaluation. Baseline
wall time was much larger than CPU time, so the wall-time ratio cannot be
attributed entirely to the code change. There are no repeats from which to
estimate timing variability and no complete multistart measurement. A table
is sufficient for these two scalar timings; plotting them would not estimate
a timing distribution or clarify the exact equality comparison.

The six baseline probe states are retained in
[baseline-state-profile.csv](results/baseline-state-profile.csv). Their three
paired speciation states have zero absolute difference between shared and
separate actions. The three pressure controls were timed but this probe did
not compare their derivatives; the complete initial Jacobian comparison above
does compare those consumed rows between wheels.

## Bound-set verification and unresolved case

The measured candidate's coupled manufactured bound-start case reaches cost
0.0020816903804324652, compared with 0.002081690380433803 from the scalar fit
with dispersion energy fixed at its upper bound. The fitted interaction
parameter is -0.027772139946327108 versus -0.027772140767741173 in the reduced
fit. Its maximum projected gradient is 7.2560e-10, below the unchanged 1e-6
criterion, and feasibility passes. Exact rows and comparison tolerances are
in [native-4235074a.csv](results/native-4235074a.csv).

The first release check stopped before fitting. Row-specific diagnosis found
coincident phases at the cold 180 K bubble seed, with the same behavior at
190 K and in the 180 K vapor composition row. The interior manufactured
reference has distinct phases. Its measured pressure, compositions and
packing fractions provide explicit starting guesses that give available
predictions and actions at the unchanged initial parameters. The corrected
check retains its +0.1 interaction coefficient start, bounds, observations
and tolerances; it recovers dispersion energy 150.00000000002808 K against
150 K and cost 1.7234876947455287e-24 against zero.

Restoring only the old callback's round-ending predicate leaves constrained
cost 0.0031494214595652998 against the same reduced reference
0.002081690380433803, failing the unchanged numerical criterion under the
same twelve-step work limit. The corrected predicate passes. This establishes
the stale-set previous-failure check; the separate release check also passes.
Neither result attributes MEA's
historical plateau to that defect. The final comparisons are retained in
[bound-case-comparisons.csv](results/bound-case-comparisons.csv).

## Failed promotion preserves valid residual results

A separate native numerical probe uses the declared methane/ethane bubble
states at 170 and 180 K, feed amounts 0.5 mol each, a pressure guess of
100000 Pa, artificial observed pressure 1000000 Pa, difference scale 1 Pa and
weights 1 and 0.25. The first-component dispersion energy is 148 K, with
affine origin 148 K, finite coordinate scale 1e308 K and unchanged physical
bounds 140–170 K. These artificial observations test numerical
representability; they are not experimental data.

The initial residual-only evaluation predicts pressures 1259949.2294408893
and 1701207.9280178961 Pa, with finite weighted cost 95248370732.84993.
Exact physical pressure derivatives remain finite at -42933.861874661874 and
-53187.822635583216 Pa/K. Multiplication by the finite but extreme coordinate
scale makes the first optimizer Jacobian entry nonfinite. The evaluator
returns the typed cause `optimizer Jacobian not finite` at row zero for a
Jacobian request. A later residual-only request at the same point retains
every prediction, residual, weighted residual and cost exactly unchanged.

At changed physical energy 149 K, the pressures are 1217790.9384003202 and
1648910.7999990298 Pa. Fresh scalar owners differ by 4.1909515857696533e-9 and
4.6566128730773926e-10 Pa, within the unchanged 1e-10 relative comparison.
Compile and central-solve counts are each 2, 0, 0 and 2 across the initial
residual call, failed promotion, retained residual call and changed-point call.
Those counts measure saved work; they are not numerical correctness criteria.

[residual-promotion-values.csv](results/residual-promotion-values.csv) owns
the exact rows. [residual-promotion-diagnostic.json](results/residual-promotion-diagnostic.json)
retains the cause, source and archive hashes and limits. The
[native probe source](scripts/residual-promotion-probe.cpp) and
[compile/run command](scripts/run-residual-promotion-probe.py) retain the
calculation. This is native code verification against the unchanged final
owner and its native archive, with the installed wheel identity recorded.
It is distinct from the installed-wheel MEA replay and qualifies this
representability failure only. The uncomputed optimizer-Jacobian entry in
the failure row table is blank, not a zero derivative.

The source review found no demonstrated calculation defect in state identity,
model lifetime, observable projection or accepted-gradient membership updates.
Independent delivered review supports the corrected source and these bounded
numerical results. The corrected tree uses Properties 4223, `regression` 1300
and total 18556 lines, equal to the hard ceilings explicitly approved by the
owner on 2026-09-29 in the [budget amendment](../../docs/scientific/code-budgets.md).
Consolidating the weighted-gradient calculation and state membership removes
ten readable runtime lines. All scientific requirements remain unchanged.
The source-only affected check passes with soft-ceiling warnings; it performs
no wheel build or numerical replay. Corrected native fitting checks
pass in 22.11 s and the native observation checks pass in 1.56 s; the
complete installed-wheel gate passes: 107 Python checks, six native groups,
packet validation, typing, source checks, analysis layout and architecture.
The installed wheel remains `28181e72` with all 14 RECORD hashes verified.
[verification.json](results/verification.json) records the bounded gate commands,
counts, wheel identity and log hashes.

The bounded Engine calculation is supported for the retained inputs; merge
approval and the explicit application handoff remain pending. Each application
must qualify its own fits or process calculations on the supplied immutable
wheel. A changed runtime requires a new wheel identity and applicable verification.
The retained distinct feeds, loadings and pressure guesses satisfy the bounded
changed-input comparison. Exhaustive combinations of physical declarations
remain outside the measured domain. F05 density-root
reuse and the other original #129 levers are separate remaining deliveries.
The first complete gate found one stale recorded native variance factor from
an older wheel. At the five-observation, two-coordinate manufactured recovery,
current native and public calculations both return dimensionless variance
factor 3.8844526205205044e-27 and final cost 5.826678930780756e-27. The variance
factor equals the weighted residual sum of squares divided by three remaining
degrees of freedom. Updating only the 28 `r4/` native fitting rows and their
case-specific provenance resolves the comparison at its unchanged relative
tolerance; every runtime calculation and assertion remains unchanged. The
[reference rows](../../engine/tests/oracle/native-rows.tsv) and
[recording provenance](../../engine/tests/oracle/native-rows.json) retain the
current operands separately from unchanged older cases. This near-zero
manufactured residual is numerical verification, not an experimental variance
estimate or physical validation.

## Initial preparation after admission

On the same frozen 84-state, 160-target point, consuming the admitted model and
compiled problems removes 84 repeated compilations. The total compile count
falls from 216 to 132; the 132 solve calls and all numerical rows remain
unchanged. The weighted objective remains 40.20153733056146, with no trial
failures. Three interleaved baseline/candidate pairs measure the change under
shared-host contention, using process user plus system time as the primary
measure and wall time as secondary evidence.
This reduces initialization work; it does not establish a per-iteration or
full-calibration speedup.

This slice reads only the frozen Engine inputs, the Engine-owned Khudaida
parameter packet and source feeds, and Engine checks. It does not read or run
an application checkout. The implementation base is `5c65bcb4`; its runtime
source is identical to `8c670d3a` and the qualified `28181e72` wheel. The
candidate wheel SHA-256 is
`659b2606737be0c66b4bc764aee3adda2b4e983b8196659b8a824955a5fd47c0`.
[performance.py](scripts/performance.py) and [replay.py](scripts/replay.py)
retain the calculation; the before/after summaries identify the wheel and
input hashes. Each heavy command uses the shared `/tmp/t3-heavy-check.lock`,
scheduling priority 10, one OpenMP and BLAS thread, two permitted build jobs
and a bounded timeout. The lock serializes the heavy steps; requested thread
settings do not prove that every unrelated host process was idle.

### Measured costs and selected change

The regular trace subtracts each child span from its parent to report exclusive
cost. Inclusive durations overlap and are not summed. The separate
[pinned-Hessian and packing probe](scripts/pinned-hessian-packing-profile.cpp)
forwards every call to the immutable wheel's original implementation and adds
its native trace scopes. Its complete output rows match the uninstrumented
wheel exactly. The probe depends on the inspected wheel's C++ ABI and unchanged
trace layout; its results apply to that wheel and source snapshot. The
interposed scopes add timing overhead, so their durations bound the removable
subset conservatively.

| Remaining lever at the frozen fit point | Measured cost | Share | Meaning of the bound |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| F05 validation preparation | Median 2.987 s | 12.3% | A second compile of each of the 84 same-model problems is removable |
| Pinned constraint Hessians | 1.854 s in 228 calls | 7.7% | Entire measured bucket; exact third derivatives remain required |
| Optimizer fixed cost | At most 0.690 s | At most 2.9% | Remaining exclusive driver time also includes other untraced work; not an isolated MUMPS or initialization measurement |
| F15 repeated packing coefficient | At most 0.003852 s | Below 0.02% | All 7,773 coefficient calls, including required calls, bound the repeated subset |
| F15 charge-vector copy | No such operation in this source | 0 | `species_z()` is absent; charge access uses the parameter vector directly |

The first row comes from three regular repeats; the instrumented rows are one
additional profiling run. [before-fit-profile.csv](results/before-fit-profile.csv)
and [native-before-fit-profile.csv](results/native-before-fit-profile.csv)
own the values. The 36% pinned-Hessian share from the earlier issue does not
apply to this input set and wheel. F05 density-observation root batches are
not exercised: every frozen target is a partial pressure or mole fraction, and
the Khudaida workload contains no density regression observations.

The change retains admission's immutable model and compiled groups through
the first evaluation. It consumes them only if every active physical value
matches the bounded affine map exactly. Otherwise it rebuilds at the actual
optimizer point and clears the discarded centers. A same-point cold retry may
reuse the same compiled problem. The solved-state, derivative, failed-trial
and successful-cache owners remain unchanged. Two single-use objective helpers
are folded into their caller with the same row-ordered sum, one final factor
of one half, and the same first-overflow causes. Regression is 1,298 lines and
the total is 18,554, each two lines below its hard ceiling; Properties and
Bindings are unchanged. No budget amendment is needed.

[ALG-FIT](../../engine/docs/science/algorithms.md#alg-fit) records the ownership
and invalidation rule. The fitting equations, reference transfer, derivative
actions, Ipopt driver, numerical policies, bounds, observations and weights
are explicitly revalidated rather than changed.

error is zero and the maximum raw row residual is 5.57e-14. These are numerical
verification on a declared local branch, not physical validation or a
phase-discovery certificate.

The preliminary equilibrium median is 0.332 s before and 0.350 s after,
within the observed 0.322–0.360 s range. Its source path is unchanged; no
equilibrium speedup is claimed. The remaining exclusive driver bound for this workload
is 0.038 s (12.1%), while all packing-coefficient calls total 3.66e-5 s.
There are no pinned phases in this workload.

### Interleaved measurements under contention

Each workload alternates baseline and candidate in three A/B pairs, with a
fresh process and verified immutable wheel for each run. The measured scope
includes the same traced native fit or equilibrium/action work on both wheels;
imports, input construction, wheel installation and CSV writing are excluded.
CPU time is process user plus system time. The load average is sampled at the
beginning and end of that scope, with its 1, 5 and 15 minute values retained.

| Pair | Fit baseline CPU, s | Fit candidate CPU, s | Fit baseline / candidate wall, s | Khudaida baseline / candidate CPU, s | Khudaida baseline / candidate wall, s |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 24.398 | 21.766 | 24.573 / 22.132 | 0.343 / 0.336 | 0.343 / 0.336 |
| 2 | 30.687 | 21.532 | 34.311 / 21.559 | 0.372 / 0.376 | 0.374 / 0.386 |
| 3 | 29.253 | 28.090 | 35.824 / 36.595 | 0.369 / 0.344 | 0.369 / 0.347 |

[paired-fit-timing.csv](results/paired-fit-timing.csv) and
[paired-equilibrium-timing.csv](results/paired-equilibrium-timing.csv) own the
full-precision times, separate user/system times, wheel hashes and load values.
[paired-performance-summary.json](results/paired-performance-summary.json)
records the statistic and command scopes. Three repeats do not estimate a
full-campaign distribution.

The fit's paired CPU reductions are 10.8%, 29.8% and 4.0%. The median of the
three within-pair CPU ratios is 1.121, an observed 10.8% reduction. The ratio of
separate sample medians would mix unequal contention and is not used. One-minute
load ranges from 3.55 to 15.50 on the two-CPU host. The owner reports concurrent
external fitting and Lithium work, including jobs outside the shared lock.
The unusually expensive second baseline and the highly contended third pair
remain in the record. Contention can affect CPU cost through shared caches and
processor frequency as well as wall time; the full observed spread cannot be
assigned to the code change. Removing 84 repeated compilations is the structural
result. The paired measurements support lower initial CPU cost on these inputs,
with a variable effect under this host load. No wall-time speedup is claimed.

The equilibrium paired CPU changes range from 1.3% slower to 6.7% faster, with
one-minute loads of 9.15–10.43. Its runtime path is unchanged, and no equilibrium
speedup is claimed. Every paired fit and equilibrium run matches the same
retained binary64 numerical rows exactly. Compilation counts remain 216 to 132
for every fit pair, with 132 solves on both wheels.

### Affine-rounding case

A separate initial evaluation uses six retained states and nine targets,
changing only the first coordinate's affine origin to 1e6. Binary64 arithmetic
resolves the first interaction coefficient to -0.06655083317309618 instead
of the input -0.06655083320547248. The immutable baseline uses the resolved
point, giving weighted cost 0.7812681271116075. The candidate returns exactly
the same predictions, residuals, weighted residuals, both Jacobians and physical
point. This probes rebuilding when admission's parameter point differs from
the actual affine point; it is not a new physical model or a calibration.
[before-affine.csv](results/before-affine.csv) owns the rows, with the exact
point and termination in [before-affine.json](results/before-affine.json) and
[candidate affine summary](results/after-affine-summary.json). Its profile
retains the same compilation count rather than bypassing the required rebuild.

The candidate passes `bash tools/check-all.sh` (107 Python checks and its
required fast native groups), the native `equilibrium`, `boundary` and
`regression_fit` programs, and `bash tools/run-slice.sh khudaida`. The source
gate and budgets also pass. A fresh Codex GPT-6.1 Sol high reviewer, applying
`cse:review` to commit `7b02aa8a` against `5c65bcb4`, returns **Supported** for
both capability and result, with no required defect identified. It inspected
the retained numerical evidence, verified logs and rendered content without
heavy replays. The numerical and contention limits above remain binding;
graphical browser layout was not checked.
[preparation-review.json](results/preparation-review.json) retains the verdict
and task identity. [preparation-verification.json](results/preparation-verification.json) records
the commands and log hashes. Public scalar
prediction preparation, density-root action-batch reuse, the pinned-Hessian
path optimization, optimizer fixed-cost alternatives and redundant packing
remain open; this slice does not close the performance issue.
